wave: R4.3.7 -- third stack-overflow vector (if/else-if chains) and an explicit statement of acknowledged incompleteness

corrects.policy: Historical evidence is immutable; r4.3.5 and r4.3.6 evidence files are left unmodified. This record supersedes their conclusions, per RECURSIVE-SELF-CENSUS.md's 'monotonic evidence, revisable conclusions' rule.

original_claim: r4.3.6's overall_verdict describes the combined bracket+operator-chain metric as closing 'the second confirmed vector', explicit that further untested constructs remain a named limitation -- but did not anticipate finding a third vector in the very next round of the SAME falsification exercise, nor had verified whether a keyword-driven (rather than symbol-driven) construct could bypass the metric entirely.
discovered_flaw: Continuing the standing loop's own mandated adversarial-input falsification practice past r4.3.6 (exactly as r4.3.6's own recensus_scope entry anticipated might be necessary), an `if x==0 {0} else if x==1 {1} else if x==2 {2} ... else {-1}` chain was tested. Its bracket-nesting depth is only 2 (each arm's `{}` pair is a SIBLING of the next, not nested inside it -- Rust's grammar makes `else` introduce a new `Expr::If` as the ELSE BRANCH of the previous one, so the AST nests one level per arm even though the braces do not), and it contains no operator-continuation characters at all (`if`/`else` are bare keywords). max_structural_recursion_risk (r4.3.6) therefore reported a risk of only 3 for a 3,000-arm chain -- and reproduced the identical SIGABRT stack-overflow crash in an isolated real process (n=3,000 crashed; not independently re-calibrated to a finer floor since the pattern was already unambiguous and the fix approach -- keyword-run counting -- generalizes cheaply regardless of the exact floor).

design_decisions.question: Track 'else' keyword occurrences as a resettable run, like chain_run, or as a simple monotonic count?
design_decisions.decision: A run, reset at ';' (a real statement boundary) and at 'fn ' (a coarse function-boundary proxy) but deliberately NOT at brace boundaries (`{`/`}`) or newlines -- chain arms are textual siblings across brace boundaries, and an adversary could otherwise evade a per-line or per-brace check by formatting. Not resetting at every brace does mean a large file containing MANY separate, small, unrelated if/else statements across one function without intervening ';' could in principle accumulate risk unrelated to any single real recursive chain -- accepted as a conservative (over-cautious) trade-off consistent with this whole heuristic's design: it may reject some benign input it doesn't need to, but must never fail to reject a genuinely pathological one.

design_decisions.question: Keep hunting for a fourth, fifth, ... vector before shipping this fix?
design_decisions.decision: No -- explicitly stopped here. Three real, distinct vectors found in direct succession (brackets, operator chains, else chains) is itself strong evidence that an ad-hoc syntax-unaware text scan cannot be made exhaustive against an open-ended space of keyword-driven and symbol-driven recursive grammar constructs. Continuing to chase individual constructs one at a time has diminishing security value relative to the effort, and risks 'narrowing scenario coverage to fake convergence' in the opposite direction (endlessly patching symptoms while implicitly claiming completeness never earned). Per RECURSIVE-SELF-CENSUS.md's own false-convergence list and this task's explicit instruction to use UNVERIFIED/PARTIALLY_MODELED-style honesty rather than false CLOSED claims, this generation instead documents the residual risk explicitly and names the two real complete-fix options (patch/fork syn to add internal stack-growth hooks, or replace whole-file parsing with a from-scratch depth-bounded parser) as future work not attempted this wave.

overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED FOR THREE SPECIFIC, EMPIRICALLY-CONFIRMED VECTORS; EXPLICITLY NOT CLAIMED COMPLETE. Closes the third real vector found by continued adversarial testing (if/else-if chains) with the same combined metric and threshold. Deliberately stops the construct-by-construct hunt here and states the residual risk plainly, per the standing loop's own explicit demand to use honest epistemic states (UNVERIFIED/PARTIALLY_MODELED) rather than fake convergence via narrowed scenario coverage -- three real vectors found in direct succession is itself the evidence that this approach cannot be assumed exhaustive.
